questions.q: What is the first phase of the incident response lifecycle?
questions.explain: Preparation precedes the incident: playbooks, roles, tools, exercises. Without it, subsequent phases are improvised.

questions.q: A workstation hosts an in-memory implant. The team wants to power it off immediately. What is the main risk?
options: The workstation will reboot too quickly
Volatile memory will be lost, along with the primary evidence
The firewall will block the reboot
The antivirus will delete the implant
questions.explain: Powering off erases memory and therefore the fileless implant, connections, and execution artifacts. You should isolate the network and then capture memory.

questions.q: What is the deliverable of the detection and analysis phase?
options: A qualified ticket with severity and initial scope
questions.explain: Detection establishes facts and qualifies the incident: true/false positive, severity, scope, escalation. It does not yet decide the full response.

questions.q: Which phase removes the root cause and the attacker's access?
questions.explain: Eradication removes access, patches the vulnerability, and rebuilds compromised systems. Containment limits spread.

questions.q: Why verify the integrity of a backup before restoring?
options: Because a compromised backup could reinstall the ransomware or implant
Because the law always requires it
questions.explain: Restoring without checking can reintroduce the compromise. The backup must be tested and its integrity confirmed.

questions.q: Which role coordinates the incident, arbitrates priorities, and handles communication?
questions.explain: The incident commander coordinates and arbitrates. Without them, decisions conflict and actions are duplicated.

options: A full technical simulation on live systems
A guided discussion of a scenario without touching systems
questions.explain: A tabletop tests decisions and coordination through discussion. A simulation executes actions and tests tools.

questions.q: What is the most important deliverable of a tabletop exercise?
options: A list of unverified assumptions and ambiguous decisions
Proof that the team responded well
questions.explain: A tabletop reveals gaps in understanding and unclear roles. These findings become dated corrective actions.

questions.q: What is the correct order of volatility for evidence collection?
questions.explain: Capture what disappears fastest first: memory, then network, then disk, then backups.

questions.q: What does the chain of custody document?
options: Who collected and handled each piece of evidence, when, and with what hash
questions.explain: Chain of custody tracks collection and handling. A break in the chain can make evidence contestable.

questions.q: A personal data breach is discovered on Monday at 10:00. What is the GDPR deadline to notify the supervisory authority?
questions.explain: GDPR requires notification within 72 hours of awareness, unless there is no risk. You notify with available information without waiting for the investigation to finish.

questions.q: What does a legal hold mean in the context of an incident?
options: Suspending the destruction of potentially relevant data
questions.explain: A legal hold suspends automatic deletions and destruction as soon as litigation or an investigation is foreseeable.

questions.q: What is the difference between an immediate cause and a root cause?
options: The immediate cause is the visible event; the root cause is the condition that made it possible
The root cause is always technical
questions.explain: 'The server was encrypted' is immediate. 'A service account without MFA allowed exposed RDP access' is the root condition.

questions.q: Match each phase to its primary deliverable.

pairs.right: PIR report and dated action items

questions.explain: Each phase produces a verifiable artifact. A PIR without dated action items is just a story.

questions.q: Which elements must appear in a post-incident report? (Select all that apply)
options: Corrective actions with owner and due date
The names of people to discipline
questions.explain: The PIR documents facts, root cause, and actions. It is not meant to assign blame: searching for individual fault blocks lessons learned.
